paragraphs.title: Building a New Place and a Miraculous Recovery

answers: Build a larger place to dwell
Capture a city
Search for the king of Syria
easy.explanation: They said that the place where they dwelt was too narrow and asked to make a larger place.
easy.q: What did the sons of the prophets ask to do near Jordan?

answers: A horse
An axe head
A beam
easy.explanation: The axe head fell into the water.
easy.q: What did one of the sons of the prophets lose while cutting wood?

answers: Go to Samaria
Return the wood
Take it up
easy.explanation: Elisha said, “Take it up to thee,” and the man put out his hand and took it.
easy.q: What did Elisha tell the man to do after the iron swam?

answers: Because the place where they dwelt was too narrow
Because the king of Israel commanded them
Because they had no water
medium.explanation: They said, “The place where we dwell with thee is too strait for us.”
medium.q: Why did the sons of the prophets want to move to a new place?

answers: He sent the prophets home
He saw the place, cut down a stick, and cast it into the water
He built a bridge over Jordan
medium.explanation: Elisha saw the place, cut down a stick, and cast it in; then the iron did swim.
medium.q: What did Elisha do after asking, “Where fell it?”

answers: A piece of wood
A water vessel
A large stone
medium.explanation: In this context, a beam is a piece of wood used in building.
medium.q: In the KJV passage, what is a “beam”?

answers: He asked Elisha to go with them
He said that it was borrowed
He stayed beside the river
challenge.explanation: He cried, “Alas, master! for it was borrowed,” showing that it did not belong to him.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the man especially needed the lost axe head?

answers: The iron swam, then they cut wood, and finally they asked for a new place
They asked for a new place, cut wood, and the axe head fell into the water
Elisha told him to take up the iron, and afterward it fell
challenge.explanation: First they asked to enlarge their dwelling, then they cut wood, and afterward the axe head fell.
challenge.q: What is the correct order of events?

answers: He ignored the problem
He solved the problem by a miracle
He told the man to buy a new axe
challenge.explanation: The iron sank in the water, but after Elisha acted, it swam.
challenge.q: What does the account emphasize about Elisha’s response to the lost axe head?

answers: Israel
Egypt
The sons of the prophets
easy.explanation: The passage says that the king of Syria warred against Israel.
easy.q: Against whom did the king of Syria war?

answers: Ben-hadad
One of the king of Syria’s servants
Elisha, the man of God
easy.explanation: Elisha sent warnings to the king of Israel about the places where the Syrians had come down.
easy.q: Who warned the king of Israel about the ambushes of Syria?

answers: Samaria
Dothan
Jordan
easy.explanation: When the king learned where Elisha was, he was told, “Behold, he is in Dothan.”
easy.q: To which city was the army sent to capture Elisha?

answers: To build a camp there
To capture Elisha
To help the king of Israel
medium.explanation: The king of Syria learned that Elisha was revealing his plans and sent an army to fetch him.
medium.q: Why was the Syrian army sent to Dothan?

answers: He avoided the places about which Elisha warned him
He left Israel
He sent his army to Dothan
medium.explanation: The king sent to the places named by the man of God and saved himself there, “not once nor twice.”
medium.q: What did the king of Israel do because of Elisha’s warnings?

answers: They had come and taken their positions
They were returning home
They were asking for water
medium.explanation: The Syrians had come down to a place to establish an ambush or camp.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “come down” mean when describing the Syrians?

answers: The Syrian army never reached Samaria
The king of Israel repeatedly avoided the ambushes
The sons of the prophets captured Dothan
challenge.explanation: The king of Israel saved himself at the warned places “not once nor twice.”
challenge.q: What caused the king of Syria to think that someone in Israel was revealing his plans?

answers: Horses, chariots, and a great host were sent
Only one man was sent
Only the sons of the prophets were sent
challenge.explanation: The king of Syria sent horses, chariots, and a great host to Dothan.
challenge.q: Which detail emphasizes the size of the force sent against Elisha?

answers: Elisha warned the king of Israel, the king of Syria learned this, and he sent an army to Dothan
The king of Israel sent an army to Dothan, so Elisha warned Syria
The king of Syria warned Elisha, so the king of Israel was safe
challenge.explanation: Elisha foiled the ambushes, the king of Syria learned of it, and he acted to capture Elisha.
challenge.q: What is the correct sequence of causes and results?

paragraphs.title: The Fiery Army and Mercy Toward the Enemy

answers: The army of Israel
The army of Syria
Mountains full of horses and chariots of fire
easy.explanation: After Elisha prayed, the servant saw the mountain full of horses and chariots of fire around Elisha.
easy.q: What did Elisha’s servant see around the city?

answers: Open his eyes
Close his eyes
Turn his eyes toward Samaria
easy.explanation: Elisha prayed, “LORD, I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see.”
easy.q: What did Elisha ask the LORD to do for his servant?

answers: They were to be killed
They were to be fed and sent away
They were to be forced back to Dothan
easy.explanation: Elisha commanded that bread and water be set before them, and then they were sent away.
easy.q: What did Elisha command to be done to the Syrian soldiers after they were brought to Samaria?

answers: Because those with Elisha were more than those with the enemy
Because the Syrian army had already left
Because the king of Israel had arrived to help
medium.explanation: Elisha said, “They that be with us are more than they that be with them.”
medium.q: Why did Elisha tell his servant, “Fear not”?

answers: They found the way themselves
Elisha led them after they were smitten with blindness
The king of Israel invited them
medium.explanation: Elisha told them to follow him and led them to Samaria after they had been struck with blindness.
medium.q: How did the Syrian soldiers come to Samaria?

answers: An inability to see properly
Defeat by weapons
Confusion caused by singing
medium.explanation: The soldiers could not see properly, so Elisha was able to lead them to another place.
medium.q: What does “blindness” mean in the passage?

answers: He hid them and then drove them away
He prevented them from seeing, but then commanded that they be fed rather than killed
He sent them to fight against Israel
challenge.explanation: Elisha used a miracle to bring them to Samaria, but chose mercy instead of slaughter.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in Elisha’s treatment of the Syrian soldiers?

answers: He was asking permission to kill the soldiers
He wanted Elisha to leave Samaria
He did not know who the soldiers were
challenge.explanation: The king saw the soldiers and asked whether he should smite them.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the king of Israel’s question, “My father, shall I smite them?”

answers: First the servant’s eyes were opened, and later the eyes of the Syrian soldiers were opened
First the king’s eyes were opened, and later Elisha’s eyes were opened
First the soldiers’ eyes were opened, and later the servant’s eyes were opened
challenge.explanation: The servant first saw the fiery army, and later the Syrian soldiers saw that they were in Samaria.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that there were two miracles involving sight?

answers: The king of Israel
Ben-hadad king of Syria
One of the sons of the prophets

answers: There was a great famine
It was full of food
It had been abandoned without a siege

answers: He rent his clothes
He left the city
He sent food to Syria
easy.explanation: The king rent his clothes, and the people saw that he had sackcloth upon his flesh.
easy.q: What did the king of Israel do after hearing the woman’s story?

She wanted to leave Samaria
She wanted to build a house upon the wall
medium.explanation: The severe famine had brought her to a desperate condition, so she cried to the king.
medium.q: Why did the woman cry to the king for help?

answers: He thought Elisha was responsible for the situation or could not solve it
Elisha had taken his throne
Elisha had refused to go to war
medium.explanation: The king swore to kill Elisha, although the passage does not say that Elisha caused the famine.
medium.q: Why was the king angry with Elisha?

answers: A garment showing mourning and distress
A container for storing water
A suit of battle armor
medium.explanation: Wearing sackcloth was a sign of mourning, sorrow, or distress.

answers: The shortage was mild and temporary
The famine was so extreme that the women discussed eating their children
The women found plenty of food in the city
challenge.explanation: The account describes such extreme distress that one child was boiled and eaten.
challenge.q: What does the story of the two women show about the severity of the famine?

answers: Elisha had found an immediate solution
The situation seemed extremely desperate, and there was little hope of prompt help
The king of Syria had lifted the siege
challenge.explanation: Elisha described the evil as being from the LORD and questioned what reason remained to wait for further help.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the words, “What should I wait for the LORD any longer?”

answers: The siege caused famine, the famine led to the shocking story, and the king blamed Elisha
Elisha caused the siege, and then the king of Syria rent his clothes
The women ended the siege, and then the city was left without a king
challenge.explanation: Ben-hadad besieged Samaria, the famine became extreme, and the king reacted in anger against Elisha.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the development of the crisis?
